summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure was admitted after a fall from stairs, sustaining multiple right rib fractures, a lumbar spine fracture, and a small pneumothorax. He developed contrast-induced acute kidney injury on baseline CKD stage 4, leading to oliguria and toxic-metabolic encephalopathy. A temporary hemodialysis catheter was placed, and he underwent intermittent dialysis with subsequent renal recovery. A Citrobacter koseri infection in the transplanted kidney was treated with ceftriaxone followed by oral ciprofloxacin. His recurrent C. difficile colitis was managed with a continued vancomycin taper. Confusion resolved with dialysis and antibiotic treatment. He improved clinically, was weaned off dialysis, and discharged to extended care with plans for transplant follow-up, fecal transplant evaluation, and completion of antibiotic and vancomycin tapers.
